entries.parameter: Focal ratio at the slicer / slit (coude focus)
entries.how: D95 gives the coude beam as f/37.5. Barlow et al. print "f/31.5" in the same sentence as a 710 um/arcsec plate scale; 3.893 m x 31.5 = 122.6 m would give 0.594 mm/arcsec, whereas f/37.5 gives 0.708 mm/arcsec, so f/31.5 is a misprint (CONFLICT, see below). The AAT coude top end is nominally f/36 (UMC1); 1.40 arcsec/mm gives f/37.7. Recommended F = 37.5.

entries.parameter: Slice width, entered as the slit
entries.how: 30 um / 0.7078 mm per arcsec = 0.0424 arcsec (with the manual's 712 um per arcsec: 0.0421). Cross-check: the 1.5 arcsec side of the entrance aperture cut into 35 slices is 1.5/35 = 0.0429 arcsec = 30.3 um. The manual's "40 um = 0.0588 arcsec" slit is a different relation (0.68 mm/arcsec) and refers to the slit mode, not the slicer. The slicer's 35 slices are one object; the explorer's single 0.0424 arcsec slit represents them.

entries.value: lens: one 300 mm fused-silica singlet, aspheric, in double pass just in front of the echelle (the same lens is the first element of the camera)
entries.how: Littrow-lens design after Gillingham's 1987 temporary spectrograph. The lens slides with the echelle on rails (450 mm travel) to refocus from 3000 to 11000 A (a singlet: chromatic).

entries.value: lens used in double pass at near-Littrow, in-plane beam separation 2 deg; the slicer is NOT in the returning beam (a secondary diverging lens intercepts the return). Verdict: not an on-axis mirror; the explorer should draw a lens (col lens, dpass) with no colTilt issue
entries.how: The returning beam "converges as it returns towards the slicer" but is picked off by the secondary collimator 2.13 m from the slit (MEASURED), the slicer aperture sits about 60 mm off the optical axis, and the TV guider picks up the reflection from the dekker plate beside it. A lens has no central obscuration, so the Schmidt-type gate (slit in the returning beam) does not apply. INFERRED because no document states "off-axis" in those words.

quotes.text: The beam separation at the echelle grating is only 2

entries.how: The lens's own focal length is not published. MEASURED from Fig. 9 the slicer-to-lens distance is 4.94 m (the lens is a telephoto-like partner of the diverging beam expander, so this is not f_col). The effective value follows from F = 37.5 and the beam W = 245.6 mm below: f_col = 37.5 x 245.6 = 9211 mm.

entries.how: Not published. Three pieces bracket it: a beam that just fills the 408 mm echelle is 408 x cos(64.95+1.0 deg) = 166 mm; "overfill ... by 25 per cent" of the 204 mm width gives 255 mm (INFERRED reading; the paper does not say 25% of what); the lens is 300 mm across. W is fixed by two sourced numbers: the slit-to-detector projection factor 0.891 (spectral, 1.0M, manual Table 1.3.1; image 1.1223 x the slit) and the camera focal length 10 339 mm (below): W = f_cam / (F x 1.1223) = 10339 / (37.5 x 1.1223) = 245.6 mm. It lies 4% under the 255 mm reading and 48% over a just-filled echelle (the footprint 245.6/cos(65.95 deg) = 604 mm exceeds the 408 mm echelle: the beam overfills it, as the paper says).

entries.parameter: Cross-disperser turn (xPsi: angle between incident and diffracted beam)
entries.how: Read from Fig. 9 (p. 328): the return beam arrives along the main axis at the turret (3.50 m from the lens), and the camera axis leaves toward the lower right: from the turret (1030, 1265 px) to the detector window (2650, 1645 px) on the 300 dpi render, atan(380/1620) = 13.2 deg. Scale: the 1 m bar spans 1924-2320 px = 396 px/m (tick centers).

quotes.text: turret center to detector window, 13.2 deg from the main axis

entries.value: 471 (V, 5909 A); ratio to the real 1200: 0.39
entries.how: The tabulated order separation ORSEP / (f_cam x FSR) gives the cross-dispersion angular dispersion the explorer must reproduce: for the V grating at order 97, 29.65 mm / (10339 mm x 60.92 A) = 4.71e-5 rad/A. A 1200 /mm grating at psi = 13 deg gives 1.24e-4 rad/A, 2.6 times too much for a camera of f_cam: the secondary collimator compresses the beam (grating beam about 0.39 x 245.6 = 96 mm, which fits a 110 mm grating). Fit: G_eff = 470.6 /mm (first order, psi = 13 deg). The same ratio q = G_eff/G comes out for the other three gratings (UV 0.401, B 0.393, V 0.392, R 0.385-0.400), which is the evidence for the compression. Re-fit if the explorer's cross-disperser formula differs.

entries.value: no order-sorting filter is needed: the cross-disperser spaces adjacent orders by 15.6 mm (3000 A) to 151 mm (11 000 A) and 29.65 mm at Na D, while the usable detector frame is 24.6 mm (Tek) and the spectrum covers only 2-15 A of a 60 A order, so one order falls on the chip; blocking filters (UG11 or BG12 in the blue, RG630 or OG530 in the red) only cut scattered light and second-order light
entries.how: For the explorer: set filt = [5878.8, 5939.7] (the free spectral range of order 97, from the A3 table, DERIVED), centered on Na D (lamC = 5890). The shortest UV spacing (15.6 mm, order 191) is smaller than the Tek frame, so at 3000 A the chip also catches the neighboring order. The single-order mode is stated in D95; a pair of flat mirrors plus narrow-band filters was the alternative way to isolate orders.

entries.parameter: Camera focal length (explorer EFFECTIVE, the whole train behind the echelle)
entries.how: Fitted to the published linear dispersion: LD = 1 / (f_cam x m / (d cos beta)) with the table's order 97 at 5909.27 A, ECH-LD = 0.13858 A/mm, d = 316 456 A, beta = 64.95 - 1.0 = 63.95 deg: f_cam = 10 339 mm. The same fit across the table varies from 9 903 mm (3001 A) to 10 546 mm (7961 A): the singlet train is not a constant-focal-length system (spread -4% / +2%). D95 calls the camera "about 10 m long". If the measured dispersion (0.1342 A/mm at 6328 A, 10% below the theory at that wavelength) is used instead, f_cam is 11 400 mm.

conflicts.detail: D95 says f/37.5; Barlow et al. (B95, p. 335) say f/31.5 with a 710 um/arcsec scale; WD85 and the manual call the coude beam f/36. Adopted f/37.5 (1.41 arcsec/mm, 0.708 mm/arcsec; the f/31.5 reading would give 0.594 mm/arcsec, not 710 um). 1.40 arcsec/mm in the manual and cookbook corresponds to f/37.7.
D95: the CIS-35 slices an area of 1.0 x 1.5 arcsec2; the manual and the AAT page: 1.5 x 1.5 arcsec. Adopted 1.5 x 1.5 (1.5/35 = 0.0429 arcsec = the 30 um slice).
About 26 (manual, 2000), about 24 (cookbook, 1999), 18 (B95, 1994 masked), 14 (D95 Fig. 3), 27 in the 1998 MITLL2 test (CBT). The mask was changed over the years; not a model parameter.

The instrument's published nominal is 1e6; recommended target 9.4e5 (the manual's "actually 940000").

Table A3 (theory): 0.1480 A/mm at 6328 A; measured 0.1342 A/mm (10% lower). The camera focal length that fits the theory is 10.34 m, the measured 11.4 m. Recommended: the theory (the manual's tables and the projection factors come from the same ray trace).
255 mm (25% over the 204 mm width, INFERRED), 245.6 mm (from the slit magnification and the camera fit, DERIVED), 166 mm (just filling the echelle). Recommended 245.6 mm.

notes: RECOMMENDED PRESET: "AAT 3.9 m / UHRF" (inst UHRF), telescope AAT 3.893 m at f/37.5. Settings: "R 940k, Tek" (1.0M: f_cam 10339 mm), "R 600k, Tek" (0.6M: f_cam 6203 mm; the nearest documented mode to R ~ 5e5), "R 300k, Tek" (0.3M: f_cam 3102 mm). All three: slit 0.0424 arcsec (the 30 um slice), D = 3.893 m, F = 37.5, W = 245.6 mm, f_col = 9212 mm, col "lens" with dpass true, cam "lens", layLen 250, camLen 4400, echelle 31.6 /mm, eDelta 64.95, gamma 0, theta 1.0, nObj 1, xd "grating" with xG 471 (EFFECTIVE; the real V grating is 1200 /mm), xPsi 13, lamC 5890 (Na D2, order 97), filt [5878.8, 5939.7], Nx 1024, Ny 1024, pix 24. Era: the Tektronix CCD of 1994-2000 (first used in 1994 April, still listed in 2000); an E2V or MITLL3 Setting (2048 x 4096, 13.5 or 15 um) would change only the chip.

PREDICTED CHECKS (not run here; the explorer must confirm): slit image 30 x 1.1223 = 33.7 um; slit-limited R = lambda / (33.7e-3 mm x 0.13858 A/mm) = 1.27e6 at 5909 A; the grating-limit R = N m = 1.25e6 (D95); in quadrature about 8.9e5, 5% below the measured 9.4e5 and 10% below the 9.9e5 of 1992-93. Pixel scale 0.0302 arcsec/px (published 0.030); dispersion 0.00333 A/px (published theory 0.13858 A/mm x 0.024 mm); order separation 29.65 mm (V grating; EFFECTIVE xG fits it).

The explorer's echelle model cannot represent: the 35-slice slicer (one slit stands for it) and its 20 mm slit length; a single lens used in double pass as collimator and first camera element, with a diverging beam expander and secondary collimator in a telephoto arrangement (the 4.94 m slit-to-lens distance versus the 9.2 m EFFECTIVE f_col; the 245.6 mm beam over-fills the 408 mm echelle: the footprint is 604 mm); the beam compression between the echelle and the cross-disperser (hence xG = 471 instead of 1200); the singlet optics' chromatic refocus (f_cam 9.9 m at 3000 A, 10.5 m at 8000 A); the cylindrical lens removed in 1994; the focal reducers and the detector carriage; one order only on a chip smaller than an order (the model draws all orders unless filt is set; filt = order 97's free spectral range).

The slit-mode alternative (0.3M with a 0.62 arcsec slit, R = 105 000, 4-5 times the slicer's throughput) is documented (UM13, CBT) but is not recommended as a preset: the slicer is the defining feature.
The Fig. 9 measurements use one 300 dpi render of the ADS scan (the rotated figure; pixel positions read to about 10 px = 0.03 m); the ADS scan prints Fig. 9 clearly but the pages are photocopies.
